A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BGPO study. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices, including the new Appendix B in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original math, coding, and planning experiments, together with gradient analyses, generalization results, and memory and training-time measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds off-policy evaluation, component ablations, and inference-length experiments.

M1.justification: V3 adds an off-policy execution of BGPO: each rollout batch of 16 is divided into two mini-batches of 8 for two successive gradient updates (Section 4.1). The sign-dependent bounds, group-based advantage, loss, and original on-policy Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MATH/GSM8K, DeepCoder training with HumanEval/MBPP evaluation, and Sudoku/Countdown. The off-policy experiments and inference-length sweep retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: The main comparator set remains diffu-GRPO and VRPO-OL, with reference results for d1-LLaDA, wd1, LLaDA-IGPO, and LLaDA-1.5. Added off-policy and one-lemma rows evaluate variants of BGPO; no external comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: V3 substantially expands the evaluation design through off-policy training with two mini-batch updates, an off-policy component-ablation protocol, and inference lengths of 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 across six benchmarks (Appendix B). The original main-experiment settings and Appendix A hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: V3 retains the MC-sample sensitivity, gradient, transfer, and efficiency analyses. It adds tests of whether both Taylor and Jensen constructions are necessary under off-policy optimization (Section 4.4, Table 3), plus inference-length robustness analysis (Appendix B, Table 6). These address substantive methodological and applicability questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain eight repeated gradient computations and the existing uncertainty displays. V3 removes the explanation that gradient standard deviations and biases are normalized by absolute parameter values, reducing statistical reporting detail. This omission does not establish a changed estimator or additional runs; the new result tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing main on-policy scores, transfer results, and timing results remain unchanged. Table 2 changes BGPO at n_t = 4 from 43.7/82.7 to 44.1/83.0 on MATH500/GSM8K. V3 substantially expands results with off-policy scores, one-lemma ablations, and length scaling. For example, off-policy BGPO scores 44.9/84.5 on math, while Table 6 reports HumanEval peaking at 48.9 with length 1024 and Countdown falling from 87.5 at length 256 to 75.4 at 2048.

T1.justification: The Taylor/Jensen lemmas, lower-bound derivations, and on-policy equivalence proof are retained. V3 corrects inconsistent summation indices in Equations 16–17 without changing the mathematical argument. Its off-policy discussion explains the existing equivalence restriction rather than introducing a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: memory-efficient optimization through sample-wise accumulation, on-policy objective and gradient equivalence, and improved math, coding, and planning performance. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 explains why objective equivalence fails off-policy and why off-policy ablation can reveal the roles of the two bounds. Appendix B newly attributes generally weaker long-generation performance to limited long-chain reasoning and context handling, although coding results show exceptions. The original limitation to 8B models remains.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code/model repository location in the abstract and explicit mini-batch/update details in Section 4.1. Appendix A's original hyperparameters remain unchanged. A new H100 reference in Section 4.3 conflicts with the retained H800 setup and Figure 1; this does not establish an actual hardware change.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are retained. V3 continues to position BGPO against single-pass likelihood approximation and memory-constrained ELBO optimization. Appendix B cites works already present in v1.

P1.justification: V3 copyedits the abstract, introduction, and technical prose, correcting wording and typographical errors. It inserts an ablation subsection, Appendix B, and acknowledgements while preserving the overall narrative and main section order.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized. Figure 1 gains off-policy bars, Table 1 gains an off-policy row and colored performance deltas, and v1 Figures 3–5 are combined into v3 Figure 3. New ablation and length-scaling tables are added, while the retained transfer and hyperparameter tables are renumbered and the appendix layout changes.

improvement.justification: The off-policy evaluation and component ablations strengthen evidence for the usefulness of both bounds, while Appendix B adds useful applicability evidence and the repository location improves access information. The core theory and main results remain stable. These gains are tempered by omitted gradient-normalization details and an overstated new claim: off-policy BGPO ties VRPO-OL at 84.8 on Countdown in Table 1, despite the text claiming superiority.
